annotation.method: Codex read the complete 47-page local PDF sequentially, including the HAL cover, all 46 printed article pages, Algorithms 1-2, Theorems 3.1-3.4, six mixed-precision strategy sections, synthetic and SuiteSparse experiments, conclusion, Appendices A-D, and references; visually checked every selected source page; searched all 24 frozen mounted object modules; and compiled private N/L proofs before accepting the targets.
annotation.reason: The project owner assigned the P19 source selection and benchmark annotation to Codex.

corpus_membership: This paper is part of the current corpus listed in metadata/manifest.json.
paper_version: HAL preprint hal-05071696v2, submitted 2026-05-19; IMA Journal of Numerical Analysis, in press, article pages 1-46

rejected_candidates.reason: These establish the computational model and hypotheses rather than a concise selected conclusion. Their four error sources are retained in T2's exact modular aggregation.

rejected_candidates.candidate: the complete asymptotic statements of Theorems 3.1-3.4
rejected_candidates.reason: Their conclusions suppress low-degree factors through the relation less-similar c(n,k), rely on detailed nonsingularity and rank hypotheses, and delegate their long proofs to Appendices A-D. T2 and T3 isolate exact, auditable mathematical content from their displayed envelopes without pretending to formalize the suppressed constants.
The rho_M and rho_b quantities make a compact exact comparison less clean. The right/flexible pair shares common terms and exposes the paper's critical implementation distinction directly.
This is a property of the synthetic matrix generator used to structure experiments, not the paper's main rounding-error contribution.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Tables 2-3 and the six strategy recommendations in Sections 4.2-4.3
rejected_candidates.reason: Several recommendations combine simplified asymptotic bounds with problem-dependent or explicitly qualified empirical behavior. T3 captures the exact theoretical right/flexible comparison that drives one of the strongest recommendations.
These report finite experiments and iteration counts rather than universally quantified mathematical results.
These are practical experiments whose outliers are explicitly noted as not always explained by the simplified theory.

rejected_candidates.candidate: backward-error, implementation-performance, and industrial-software directions in Section 6
rejected_candidates.reason: The paper identifies these as open issues or future work, not completed results.

T1.decision: Use the exact upper perturbation-norm inequality in equation (C.8), which is a direct specialization of the frozen Euclidean triangle theorem.

T2.decision: Use an exact finite-vector realization of the four weighted error sources collected in xi in equation (3.8).

T3.decision: Use exact paper-scoped forms of the right and flexible envelopes (3.17) and (3.20), then strengthen Remark 4 with gap, equality, and strictness certificates.

selection_policy: Prefer exact inequalities and comparisons over conclusions expressed only through suppressed asymptotic constants.
Represent the paper's four modular error sources and right/flexible precision distinction explicitly.
Do not promote empirical heatmaps, iteration counts, qualified recommendations, or future-work claims to theorem targets.
Keep every public definition free of NumStability imports.
Assign tiers only from the 24 modules in metadata/library_olean.json.
